newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end softer led by weak golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end softer led by weak golds.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended softer in moderate trading * Gold sector led 10 of 14 groups lower * Modest gains in banking, retailing * 75 million shares traded worth C$948 million
Toronto stocks finished softer on Monday, depressed by plummeting gold prices and quarter-end profit-taking, analysts said.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 9.97 points to close at 5291.08 in moderate turnover of 75.2 million shares worth C$948.6 million.

"The market in the last few days has been uninteresting and meandering," said Ron Meisels, president of P and C Holdings Ltd of Montreal. He said the Canadian market has enjoyed a strong run since July and may encounter more profit-taking over the next few days.
"Once the quarter is over, portfolio managers very often start to take some profits," Meisels said.
In today's action, the precious metals group led 10 of 14 sub-groups into negative territory. COMEX gold futures sank to fresh three-year lows in reaction to a strong U.S. dollar, gold traders said.
Investors also grabbed profits in consumer products, conglomerates, forestry products and real estate.
The TSE rose modestly in pipelines, energy, retailing and financial services. Despite today's gains, the banks are likely to see some profit-taking following their recent rally.
Declining stocks outnumbered advancers 513 to 442 with 257 issues ending flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Takeover target Loewen Group Ltd jumped 1.25 to 57 amid market speculation that Service Corp International will sweeten its US$48 a share offer.
* Toronto-Dominion Bank gained 0.25 at 27.65 on 1.1 million shares. The Federal Reserve earlier approved the bank's C$715 million purchase of Waterhouse Investor Services.
* Tarxien Corp added 1.40 to 11.40 after Ventra Group said it will offer C$38 million offer for the auto parts maker.
